proposed_widenings.name: create_object
proposed_widenings.justification: Fabricate's entire mechanic is transforming raw materials into a crafted product of the same material. No existing EffectAtom represents object creation from raw stock. 'alter_item_kind' is for form-switching a single existing item (Folding Boat) and carries no concept of raw-material inputs, size constraints, or proficiency gates. 'create_object' appears in the v4 taxonomy (TAXONOMY_atoms_graph.md §9 Effect Atoms) but is absent from types.ts.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You convert raw materials into products of the same material. For example, you can fabricate a wooden bridge from a clump of trees, a rope from a patch of hemp, or clothes from flax or wool.

proposed_widenings.name: ObjectFilter.material — extend beyond 'metal' | 'flammable'
proposed_widenings.justification: The object attachment filter's material enum ('metal' | 'flammable') cannot express 'raw/unprocessed material'. Fabricate targets raw stock generally. A 'raw_material' filter concept or removal of the filter restriction would be needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Choose raw materials that you can see within range.

notes: The spell fits the 'activation' family structurally (instantaneous, direct phase, 10-minute casting time which maps to CastingTime.minutes). The blocking gap is the missing 'create_object' effect atom — it exists in the v4 taxonomy but has never been surfaced in types.ts. Using 'alter_item_kind' would produce a dishonest trace: that atom models form-switching of a single existing item, not material-to-product fabrication. The size constraints (Large vs Medium for minerals) and proficiency gate (no high-skill items without Artisan's Tools proficiency) are secondary encoding concerns that would also need surface additions but are not the primary blocker.
